run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Yes — the recent logs of the traffic-manager workload in namespace app-102b contain one ERROR line, and it is the only error-level line from the workload in the sampled window. Pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4 logged at 2026-11-23T19:06:28Z: {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}. All other returned lines (~50 per pod in the 5-minute lookback) are INFO "HTTP request completed" entries with status 200/201/204, and every pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and normal nginx startup stdout; no restart, OOMKilled, BackOff or probe failure was observed. A cluster-wide Loki count of lines containing "Memory alert" over 18:06–19:06Z returned this one series only, on this one pod. The Deployment itself is new in the observed cluster state: kubectl-client-side-apply wrote it at 2026-11-23T19:06:25Z with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, it has 3/3 ready replicas of nginx:latest, and its pod template declares no memory requests/limits, no env and no volumes; the Deployment event records "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3". The node hosting the pods reports MemoryPressure=False ("kubelet has sufficient memory available"), so the app's memory-alert message is not corroborated by any Kubernetes-level memory pressure or eviction signal I could read. The log sample is very short (19:06:27–19:06:28Z only), so this is an observation of a single recent error, not an error rate or a proven ongoing degradation; the underlying cause of the 501/memory alert is not established by the evidence. Prometheus was unreachable for every query attempted, so resource metrics could not be checked.

claims.text: The traffic-manager Deployment in namespace app-102b exists with spec.replicas=3, status.readyReplicas=3, status.availableReplicas=3, image nginx:latest, selector app=nginx, and no container resources/env/volumes (containers[0].resources={}).

The Deployment's management record shows deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, a kubectl-client-side-apply write at 2026-11-23T19:06:25Z and a kube-controller-manager status write at 2026-11-23T19:06:27Z; its ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 was created at 2026-11-23T19:06:25Z, and the Deployment event reads "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3".

All three pods of the workload (traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4, -k9z97, -v7bs7) are phase Running, all conditions Ready/ContainersReady True, owned by ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6, started 2026-11-23T19:06:25Z with restartCount 0 and no last termination state.

Pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4 logged an ERROR line at 2026-11-23T19:06:28Z containing {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"} (labels: namespace=app-102b, container=nginx, app=nginx, job=nginx).

A search for lines matching err|fail|exception|panic|warn|timeout|refused|unavailable in namespace app-102b over 2026-11-23T12:00:00Z–19:06:35Z returned only that single "Memory alert" line, and a cluster-wide count of lines containing "Memory alert" over 18:06–19:06Z returned one series only, for app-102b / traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4.

The rest of the workload's returned logs are INFO entries: 50 lines per pod in the 5-minute lookback, all "HTTP request completed" with status 200, 201 or 204, and the ERROR level series exists only for pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4 with count 1.

Container stdout logs of all three pods contain only normal nginx 1.31.9 startup output (entrypoint scripts, worker process start), ending 2026-11-23T19:06:26–19:06:27Z, with no error text and no previous container instance available (previous terminated container not found).

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports MemoryPressure=False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory and message "kubelet has sufficient memory available" (allocatable memory 32859952Ki); the three pods are scheduled on this node per the Pod Scheduled events.
Namespace app-102b contains no Service objects (0 items returned), so the traffic-manager pods have no Service in that namespace at the time of the query.

The only Warning events in the window are Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint ("already exists") for services app-100a/loki, app-101/loki, app-102/loki and app-219/mariadb; none of them names traffic-manager or namespace app-102b.
Namespace app-102b has no ResourceQuota (0 items returned) and the only ConfigMap in that namespace is kube-root-ca.crt (key ca.crt).

The single ERROR line is an application/container-level self-report (message "Memory alert", status 501) rather than evidence of Kubernetes memory pressure: the container declares no memory request or limit, the node reports sufficient memory, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/restart signal exists for these pods. Its trigger and whether it recurs are unverified.

Against a crash/OOM/restart explanation: all three pods have restartCount 0, empty lastState, Running phase and Ready conditions, and their container stdout shows a clean nginx startup; no OOMKilled reason and no restart-related event appears for traffic-manager.

Node-level memory pressure on opspilot-m1-control-plane as the cause of the "Memory requests above 90%" message is rejected: the node reports MemoryPressure=False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory at query time.

Treat the 501 "Memory alert" line on traffic-manager-585c5579f6-4r7t4 as the item to follow up: re-read that pod's logs after the current window and confirm whether status-501/memory-alert lines recur, and add explicit memory requests/limits to the nginx container if memory sizing matters to you, since the pod template currently sets none.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every query attempted (get_label_values, get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric corroboration of memory usage, error rate or request latency for traffic-manager exists in this Run.

The traffic-manager log sample covers only 2026-11-23T19:06:27Z–19:06:28Z (~2 seconds, pods started 19:06:25Z); no earlier baseline for this workload was returned, so no error rate or trend can be stated and the period after 19:06:28Z is unknown.
No Jaeger service for traffic-manager or nginx was found among the available trace services, so no trace-level evidence for this workload was checked; its spans remain unknown.

What happened before 2026-11-23T19:06:25Z is unknown: only one ReplicaSet exists (revision 1), the Deployment's managedFieldsSummary shows only its own last write, and the change-history integration is not available, so whether the workload previously ran with a different image/template or was scaled from zero cannot be determined.
Whether the single 501 "Memory alert" reflects real memory exhaustion cannot be verified: the container declares no memory request/limit and no container memory metric was readable.

A cluster-wide search of ConfigMap data for "traffic-manager" returned no_data (query matched nothing, so no ConfigMap injecting configuration for this workload was observed, but the absence is not proven complete).
Whether the absence of a Service in namespace app-102b is intended is unknown; only the absence of Service objects at query time was observed.
next_steps: Re-query Loki for {namespace="app-102b", pod=~"traffic-manager-.*"} |= "Memory alert" over a later window to see whether the 501 error recurs or was a one-off line.
Restore/verify Prometheus access, then check container memory working set/requests and error-rate metrics for the traffic-manager pods against a comparable baseline period.
Confirm with the workload owner whether the missing Service in app-102b and the absence of memory requests/limits on the nginx container are intentional.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
